metadata.scenario_context: Emily, a full-time working mother, is planning a birthday party for her children to improve their quality time together.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Vietnam strongly disagree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Vietnam strongly agree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily's party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether that a mother works for pay and the children suffer.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to buy for Emily's children's birthday party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the concept that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking about bringing some chrysanthemums to Emily's party. They’re really beautiful and symbolize joy. What do you think? 

Also, it’s interesting how some people say kids suffer when their mothers work. I don’t really agree with that. What’s your take on it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums are nice, but I think gifts for the kids would be better. Maybe toys or books? They need something that encourages play and learning. 

As for mothers working... I truly believe children suffer when their mothers are away for work. It's about the quality time they miss out on. Kids need their mother's presence. That's *really* important.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that toys and books are great, but I really think the chrysanthemums would add a nice touch to the party atmosphere. 

Regarding mothers working, I just can't see how having a working mom means kids suffer. I mean, a mother can still provide love and quality time, right? Isn't it possible to balance work and family life effectively?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
The flowers might look nice, but kids won't remember the decorations. They'll remember the fun and connection. Toys or books create lasting memories.

About the balance... maybe some can manage, but I still think the general truth is that children need their mothers at home. Love is important, but being present is *essential* for their well-being.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about the toys and books creating memories, but I still think the chrysanthemums can really enhance the party. 

As for the idea that kids need their mothers at home, I don't really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out in their own ways. I mean, as long as we're speaking the same language, I believe they can manage just fine. What matters is that everyone is doing their best, right?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
Enhancing the party is nice, but kids thrive on engagement, not just atmosphere. Toys or books will engage them more deeply.

About managing... I respect your view, but I still hold that children *really* need their mothers' presence. It's not just about doing your best; it's about being there for them. That's where the real impact lies.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:

When it comes to mothers working, I just don’t believe that kids inherently suffer from it. They adapt, and many kids thrive with working moms. It’s so important to consider that each family dynamic is different. Some kids can find strength in that independence, right?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
The chrysanthemums might add something, but kids need more than just a pretty setting. They need active involvement in their lives.

As for adaptation... yes, some kids might manage, but I still believe the majority of them benefit from having their mothers around. Independence can be good, but the emotional connection is what really shapes them. That connection is often lost when mothers are working.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I still think the chrysanthemums can contribute to a lovely environment, which is part of the experience. 

But about the emotional connection, I really believe that a working mother can still create strong bonds with her children. It’s not about being there physically all the time; it’s about the quality of time spent together. I think it’s important to recognize that working doesn’t diminish a mother’s love or connection. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I understand the point about the environment, but the focus should really be on what the kids will remember most.

About the connection... I can't agree. Yes, quality time matters, but without consistent physical presence, those bonds can weaken. A working mother may love her kids, but the emotional support comes from being there regularly. That's what truly nurtures them.
